title: Peg a T-shirt onto a clothesline
instruction: Hang the T-shirt from the clothesline using the two pegs, then let go and leave it secure and clear of the table.
context: Clipping flexible clothing onto a line combines fabric handling with operating a spring clamp, a common household and assisted-living activity.
setup: Proposed fixed setup, metres in the YAM station frame: a dry cotton child-sized T-shirt, body width 0.28, hem-to-shoulder length 0.30, sleeve span 0.40, nominal 180 g/m² and 33.9 g, starts loosely draped over a fixed low plastic laundry board, 200 x 440 x 100 mm (8 mm top, four 15 mm square legs), centred at x=0.36,y=0,z=0.7975 on the 0.7475 m table. Its hem overhangs the support's near edge by 65 mm. At reset the shirt starts flat 3 mm above the support, hem x=0.195 and shoulders x=0.495, then settles under gravity for 5 seconds before the first policy action. A taut 3 mm line spans y=-0.25 to +0.25 at x=0.52,z=1.09, supported by two fixed 25 mm square posts and 150 x 70 x 15 mm feet. Two 70 x 10 x 22 mm wooden spring pegs, nominal 8 g each, start closed on ordinary stepped wooden rests, hinge centres x=0.32,y=+/-0.30,z=0.88, long axes along x. Each rest has a 90 x 60 x 8 mm base, a 35 x 16 x 125 mm jaw support and a 15 x 16 x 120.5 mm handle support; the outer 20 mm of each handle overhangs. No peg is attached to a rest. Final screenshot and reachable layout require physical validation.
scoring: Proposed: 0.5 for one peg visibly retaining the fabric and line, with the whole shirt at least 20 mm clear of the table/floor and supported only by the line and pegs for 5 seconds; 1.0 for two such pegs at least 180 mm apart. Otherwise 0. Damaged objects, false contact, hidden attachments or unphysical deformation invalidate the run. See JUDGING.md.
run_limit: Proposed: 2,400 control steps, 2 minutes at 20 Hz, including the final 5-second released hold.
reset_notes: Restore the same loose garment drape over the laundry support, closed pegs and fixed rack. Replace damaged physical fabric or pegs. The cloth reset and passive peg rests have passed separate native checks; their combined robot pickup remains under validation. Simulation initialization uses one raw environment reset followed by exactly 100 control steps (5 seconds at 20 Hz) holding the ordinary ready posture, allowing native cloth and free props to settle. This same procedure is required for every policy; the final matching setup screenshot is pending.
fidelity: Implemented native 2D surface FEM with two sewn fabric layers, self-contact and passive spring-driven rigid jaws. No proximity grasp or cloth animation. Taut line is a static cylinder. Cotton anisotropy, yarns, tearing and wetness are not modeled. Friction, bending and peg torque are uncalibrated; native contact validation is incomplete.
scores: Not evaluated. No demo or Dream score exists.
